title: UK methane fuel-supply action and flaring/venting QA controls

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: UK methane action plan accessible webpage

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Carbon budget and growth delivery plan

facts.source_fact: UK methane emissions fell by 62 percent between 1990 and 2023 according to the action plan's cited statistics.
facts.expected_handling: Keep the national territorial time-series scope.

facts.source_fact: Agriculture, waste and fuel supply together account for 87 percent of UK territorial methane emissions in the action-plan framing.
facts.expected_handling: Do not apply the combined share to an individual sector.

facts.source_fact: Fuel supply covers production, import and distribution of fuels for energy, transport, heating and industrial processes.
facts.expected_handling: Attach the fuel-supply sector boundary.

facts.source_fact: The fuel-supply scope also anticipates low-carbon and alternative fuels such as biofuels and hydrogen.
facts.expected_handling: Keep current fossil emissions separate from future-fuel policy scope.

facts.source_fact: Methane can be emitted during extraction, processing and transportation of fossil fuels.
facts.expected_handling: Track source stage before aggregation.

facts.source_fact: Methane produced with oil can be emitted if it is not captured or used.
facts.expected_handling: Distinguish captured, used and emitted gas.

facts.source_fact: Gas-distribution leakage is a material fuel-supply methane source.
facts.expected_handling: Separate network leakage from upstream oil-and-gas sources.

facts.source_fact: Upstream oil and gas accounted for less than 2 percent of UK methane emissions in 2023 in the action plan.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve year and national denominator.

facts.source_fact: The total fuel-supply sector accounted for around 8 percent of UK methane emissions in 2023.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve approximate status and reference year.

facts.source_fact: Gas-distribution leakage accounted for approximately 6 percent of UK methane emissions in the action-plan description.
facts.expected_handling: Do not add approximate shares without checking common denominator and rounding.

facts.source_fact: Fuel-supply methane emissions fell by 88 percent from 1990 to 2023.
facts.expected_handling: Keep sector and time boundaries.

facts.source_fact: The North Sea Transition Authority uses a consenting process for flaring and venting.
facts.expected_handling: Carry consent status with flaring/venting records.

facts.source_fact: The NSTA requires industry Emissions Reduction Action Plans.
facts.expected_handling: Treat action plans as governance evidence, not measured reductions by themselves.

facts.source_fact: The NSTA reports annual emissions-reduction progress and publishes asset-level benchmarking including flaring and venting.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve asset and reporting-year provenance.

facts.source_fact: NSTA estimates UK Continental Shelf flaring decreased by 51 percent between 2018 and 2024.
facts.expected_handling: Label this as an NSTA estimate with its period.

facts.source_fact: Methane and wind-sensor drones are being trialled for targeted source identification and emissions quantification.
facts.expected_handling: Treat trial measurements separately from routine inventory values.

facts.source_fact: UK upstream oil-and-gas methane intensity was 0.18 percent in 2020 in the action plan's case study.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve intensity denominator and year.

facts.source_fact: The NSTA projected methane intensity to decrease to 0.12 percent in 2024 data.
facts.expected_handling: Label the 0.12 percent figure as projected in the cited action-plan context.

facts.source_fact: Quantified fuel-supply policies plus the Energy and Emission Projections baseline contribute 15 percent of the projected UK methane reduction from 2023 to 2030.
facts.expected_handling: Do not interpret the contribution share as a sector emissions level.

facts.source_fact: UK policy and NSTA requirements target zero routine flaring and venting by 2030.
facts.expected_handling: Treat the 2030 position as a target, not a completed outcome.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve percentages, estimates, projections and targets with qualifiers.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents policy targets being reported as measured outcomes.

guard_patterns.handling: Attach national, fuel-supply, upstream, network and asset scope.
Attach base year, reference year and target year.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents stale or premature target claims.

guard_patterns.handling: Carry inventory, NSTA estimate, projection and trial-measurement provenance.
Do not convert national/asset policy statistics into parcel-level methane measurements.
